note: After Banks's (1901) original description of the new species (in English), there placed in the genus Calotermes (Calotermes pacificus sp. nov.) and later transferred to Incisitermes; both the alate and the soldier are described. The original gives no measurements of individual parts, only total lengths; the individual variation in the body length of the soldier was pointed out by the author himself.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Pale yellowish brown, the underside paler, the legs and antennae also pale; wings transparent, the costa and subcosta and their branches brown. Head not very large, the compound eyes about at the middle, ocelli present. Pronotum nearly twice as wide as long, the anterior margin concave, as wide as the head. Mesonotum and metanotum much longer than the pronotum and as wide as the head. Abdomen distinctly longer than the head and thorax together. Wings not much longer than the body, of moderate width; the costa branches both before the middle and before the apex; the media about between the subcosta and the submedia, branched proximally and connected with the subcosta; the apical branches of the submedia mostly forked, the branches towards the base very oblique.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head chestnut, darker in front than behind; mandibles black; the rest of the body, legs and antennae pale yellow. Head about 1.33 times as long as wide, the sides slightly convex, equally wide in front and behind, slightly flattened above, slightly concave above the middle near the anterior margin. Mandibles stout, with 2 small teeth near the apex and a larger tooth towards the base, and a swelling on the outer side of the base. Antennae slender, about as long as the head width, 14-segmented, segment 3 distinctly longer than the other segments and darker. Pronotum distinctly wider than long, as large as the mesonotum and metanotum together; mesonotum and metanotum only slightly separated from each other, each with a small process near the posterolateral corner. Abdomen short, slightly wider in the middle than the head.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Measurements: alate body length including the wings 11 mm, body length 8 mm; soldier body length 12 mm. Collecting: Albemarle Island, December (month 12) and February (month 2); Narboro Island, January (month 1); many specimens; some soldiers distinctly smaller with a slightly shorter head.
